newsitem.title: JAPAN: Loss-making Yamaichi reduces executive salaries.
newsitem.headline: Loss-making Yamaichi reduces executive salaries.

text.p: Japan's fourth biggest brokerage Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd said on Friday it has started reducing salaries of company executives by 10 to 25 percent to cut costs.

Yamaichi director Masatoshi Watanabe told reporters that the pay cuts, which took effect in July, would contribute to reducing some 100 million yen ($862,000) a year in the loss-making brokerage's expenditure.

Earlier on Friday, Yamaichi announced 5.43 billion yen ($46.8 million) in parent current losses for the first quarter of 1997/98 started in April. Yamaichi did not disclose the results of the first quarter a year earlier as it has just begun announcing quarterly results from 1997/98. It posted a 1.22 billion yen ($10.5 million) profit in the 1996/97 year.

Watanabe attributed the loss in the first quarter partly to a change in accounting measures for short-term securities trading and derivatives from 1997/98 and appraisal losses in dual-currency bonds which it had planned to market in May but failed to do so due to a higher yen against the dollar.

The change in accounting methods cut its trading profits by some 1.4 billion yen ($12.0 million) for the first quarter, and the appraisal loss of the dual currency bonds totalled more than two billion yen ($17.2 million), he said.
Watanabe said that Yamaichi would try hard to post profits in the first half by cutting operational costs and offering attractive financial products.
Earlier this month, Yamaichi said that it plans to reduce the number of group directors by 10-20 percent possibly next March.
In 1996/97, Yamaichi Securities suffered a parent net loss of 164.76 billion yen ($1.42 billion) to help its non-bank subsidiary dispose of problem loans. ($1=116 yen)
